records.summary_en: A military crew member saw a small object moving quickly in the opposite direction from the aircraft. When he tried to get a closer shot, the object left the camera’s field of view and could not be found again.

records.title: DOW-UAP-D091, Range Fouler Debrief, Atlantic Ocean, 2020
records.summary_en: A military crew member saw a dark, misshapen balloon-like object drifting over the ocean. The report did not identify it.

records.title: DOW-UAP-D092, Department of the Air Force Committee to Review Project Bluebook, 1966-1967
records.summary_en: The Air Force was advised to assemble a scientific team to investigate selected reports of unidentified objects. At a meeting on how to carry out the recommendation, officials couldn’t decide whether to hire a university or individual researchers.

records.title: DOW-UAP-D093, Analysis of Flying Object Incidents in the United States, 1948
records.summary_en: Workers at the Richmond Weather Bureau reported seeing objects through a theodolite on four occasions. An Air Force study failed to identify them and considered whether they might have come from the Soviet Union.

records.title: DOW-UAP-D095, Joint U.S.-Canadian Aviation Projects and UFO Sighting Reports, 1954-1955
records.summary_en: Near Newfoundland, a US aircraft crew reported seeing something in the sky as ground radar picked up a contact. An Air Force board could not explain the two reports together.

records.title: DOW-UAP-D096, Correspondence Relating to Project Blue Book, 1955
records.summary_en: Kenneth Hansen asked the Air Force for photos, pamphlets, and a letter to help convince his class that flying saucers were real. The record contains no response to his request.

records.title: DOW-UAP-PR024, Unresolved UAP Report, Middle East, 2023
records.summary_en: Two bright dots pass through footage from a military sensor and disappear. The dark area remains centered, and the screen flashes white near the end.

records.title: DOW-UAP-PR030, Unresolved UAP Report, Middle East, 2023
records.summary_en: A brief video from a military sensor shows two spots crossing the image in opposite directions. The report describes their movements but does not explain what they were.

records.title: DOW-UAP-PR100, Unresolved UAP Report, Yellow Sea, 2023
records.summary_en: A military camera over the Yellow Sea tracked a conspicuous area on screen. It disappeared and returned, and the video seemed to skip—but what it was remains unknown.

records.title: DOW-UAP-PR101, Unresolved UAP Report, South China Sea, 2024
records.summary_en: A U.S. military camera tracked an area that appeared as a line of moving marks. The marks grew less distinct as they moved farther away.

records.title: DOW-UAP-PR102, Unresolved UAP Report, East China Sea, 2024
records.summary_en: A military sensor tracked an area that looked different from its surroundings until it slipped out of frame. The video does not identify what was there.

records.title: DOW-UAP-PR103, Unresolved UAP Report, East China Sea, 2024
records.summary_en: A military sensor tracked an area that looked different from the rest of the image. A box marked it, but the record does not identify what was there.

records.title: DOW-UAP-PR106, Unresolved UAP Report, Eastern United States, 2020
records.summary_en: A small spot appeared to leap and vanish from the screen just as the sensor changed modes. The report described it as metallic but did not identify what it was.

records.title: DOW-UAP-PR107, Unresolved UAP Report, Eastern United States, 2020
records.summary_en: In a 2020 military video, a blur that looks different from the background repeatedly slips out of frame and reappears. The camera tracks it and changes its zoom, but the report does not identify what it shows.

records.title: DOW-UAP-PR108, Unresolved UAP Report, Western United States, 2020
records.summary_en: Footage from a military sensor shows a tracking marker circling a spot. It slips off the left edge of the frame, but what it was remains unclear.

records.title: DOW-UAP-PR109, Unresolved UAP Report, Eastern United States, 2015
records.summary_en: A spot appears in military footage, crosses the frame, and disappears at the corner. The video replays it in slow motion but doesn’t identify its source.

records.title: DOW-UAP-PR110, Unresolved UAP Report, Eastern United States, 2020
records.summary_en: A military sensor tracked a dark area that seemed to grow until it left the frame. The footage doesn’t reveal what it was.

records.title: DOW-UAP-PR111, Unresolved UAP Report, Eastern United States, 2020
records.summary_en: In footage from a military camera, a tracking marker surrounds a prominent area as the camera follows it. When the camera pulls back, the area disappears from view. The report does not identify it.

records.title: DOW-UAP-PR112, Unresolved UAP Report, Eastern United States, 2019
records.summary_en: Video from a sensor aboard a civilian aircraft shows a small dot moving quickly. When the sensor changes its display, the dot slips off the left side of the screen.

records.title: DOW-UAP-PR114, Unresolved UAP Report, Atlantic Ocean, 2016
records.summary_en: A military sensor tracks a distinct spot on screen, then stops tracking as the spot exits on the right. Near the end of the video, another distinct spot enters from the same side, though it is not known whether it is the same one.

records.title: DOW-UAP-PR116, Unresolved UAP Report, Atlantic Ocean, 2020
records.summary_en: A military camera tracked a dark patch over the ocean. The report described it as balloon-like and drifting with the wind, but did not identify it.

records.title: FBI-UAP-D014, Correspondence Relating to UFO Sightings, 1967, 1974
records.summary_en: A letter described a chase, a brief landing, and someone getting out to walk around. The FBI replied that it had no information about the case.

records.title: NASA-UAP-D026, Apollo 14 Debriefing, 1971
records.summary_en: The Apollo 14 crew discussed flashes of light they saw during the mission. Particles from space can pass through the eye and create the sensation of a flash.

records.title: NASA-UAP-D027, Apollo 14 Debriefing (Continued), 1971
records.summary_en: After the Apollo 14 mission, the crew revisited flashes of light. Particles from space can strike the retina, causing the brain to perceive a flash or streak of light.

records.title: NASA-UAP-D028, Apollo 17 Crew Medical Debriefing, 1972
records.summary_en: Two of Apollo 17’s three crew members reported seeing flashes of light in orbit around the Moon and on its surface. Particles from space can pass through the eye and create the sensation of light.

records.title: NASA-UAP-D029, Apollo 17 Crew Medical Debriefing (Continued), 1972
records.summary_en: Two of the three Apollo 17 crew members reported flashes of light in orbit around the Moon and on its surface. In a debriefing, they discussed the possibility that particles from space had made them see light.

records.title: DOW-UAP-D098, Film Analysis of Unidentified Objects, 1953
records.summary_en: Three groups of lights appear in the Utah footage. Two seem to merge and then separate again, and calculations of their motion don’t fit the explanations investigators considered.

records.title: FBI-UAP-D025, Digital Rendering, “Airborne Triangle,” 2002
records.summary_en: In 2026, the FBI created an illustration of a triangle over Bagram Air Base, based on a former servicemember’s account of an incident in 2002. The image is an illustration, not a photograph.

records.title: FBI-UAP-D027, Digital Rendering, “Dark Translucent Triangle,” 2023
records.summary_en: A former employee of the U.S. Department of War described an incident near Colorado Springs. In 2026, the FBI created a computer-generated illustration of a dark, semitransparent triangle based on his account.

records.title: FBI-UAP-D029, Digital Rendering, “Dark Triangle with Lights,” 2011
records.summary_en: Two former U.S. military personnel described a dark triangle with lights in the summer of 2011. In 2026, the FBI created a computer-generated image based on their account.

records.title: FBI-UAP-D031, Digital Rendering, “Large Triangle with Red Lights,” 2023
records.summary_en: The FBI created a drawing of a large triangle with red lights based on the account of someone who reported an incident near Colorado Springs. The full account appears in a separate record.

records.title: FBI-UAP-D038, Digital Rendering 1, “Multiple Red Lights,” 2026
records.summary_en: The FBI created a drawing of several red lights based on an account from two people. The record provides neither their full description nor an explanation for the lights.

records.title: FBI-UAP-D039, Digital Rendering 2, “Multiple Red Lights,” 2026
records.summary_en: Two people described several red lights in the western United States. The FBI created a drawing based on their account but did not explain what the lights were.

records.title: FBI-UAP-D041, Digital Rendering 1, “Multiple Red Lights,” 2026
records.summary_en: Two people described an incident in the western United States in 2026. The FBI created an illustration of several red lights based on their account, but the document does not say what the lights were or what caused them.

records.title: FBI-UAP-D042, Digital Rendering 2, “Multiple Red Lights,” 2026
records.summary_en: Two people described an incident in the western United States in 2026. The FBI used their account to create an illustration of several red lights, not a photograph.

records.title: CIA-UAP-D022, Unidentified Flying Object Reported near Puerto Rico, 1965
records.summary_en: A Navy pilot saw a triangular object near Puerto Rico, about the size of a fighter jet. A warship’s radar tracked it and calculated a speed of about 7,000 kilometers per hour, but the object was never identified.

records.title: CIA-UAP-D023, Briefing Notes for Mr. Walter Elder
records.summary_en: A warship’s radar tracked an object near Puerto Rico for 21 minutes. A fighter pilot saw a triangular shape, and the object approached his aircraft.

records.title: DOS-UAP-D001, Diplomatic Cable, Brazil, November 14, 1963
records.summary_en: A Brazilian newspaper reported that a balloon contained a dead man in a spacesuit. The embassy looked into the report, but understood that a weather balloon had been seen in the area and that no crashed craft had been found.

records.title: DOS-UAP-D002, Diplomatic Cable, Brazil, November 20, 1963
records.summary_en: Reports of a mysterious object brought people to Conde, but no one who had seen it could be found. A local reporter sent a telegram from there using an old Morse device.

records.title: DOW-UAP-D099, Intelligence Review of “Ghost Rocket” Incidents, 1947
records.summary_en: A Swedish pilot saw a dark object in the sky. Military officials suspected Soviet missiles, but told the public most sightings had a celestial origin. Some may have been actual missiles.

records.title: DOW-UAP-D100, Air Materiel Command Report on Unidentified Flying Objects, 1947-1948
records.summary_en: The military investigated about 180 reports of objects in the sky. Many were identified as balloons or sightings of Venus, but several remained unexplained, with no physical evidence to examine.

records.title: DOW-UAP-D101, Intelligence Information Report, Unresolved UAP Report, Gulf of Oman, 2021
records.summary_en: An aircraft crew spotted two orbs near a flare over the sea. They moved away when the gun fired, but the recording was corrupted.

records.title: DOW-UAP-PR117, Unresolved UAP Report, Gulf of Oman, 2021
records.summary_en: A phone recording of a sensor display aboard a military aircraft shows an area that looks different from its surroundings and remains near the center of the image. An accompanying report describes the phenomenon as cold spheres but does not identify it.

records.title: DOW-UAP-PR118, Unresolved UAP Report, Gulf of Oman, 2021
records.summary_en: A video recorded from a military aircraft’s display shows a blip that usually stays near the center before slipping off the bottom of the frame. A separate report called the phenomena “cold spheres,” but did not explain what they were.

records.title: DOW-UAP-PR119, Unresolved UAP Report, Gulf of Oman, 2021
records.summary_en: A phone captured a spot that stayed centered on a sensor display aboard an aircraft over the Gulf of Oman. A separate report described it as cold orbs but did not explain the basis for that description.

records.title: DOW-UAP-PR120, Unresolved UAP Report, Gulf of Oman, 2021
records.summary_en: A phone video shows a prominent spot on a sensor display aboard an aircraft over the Gulf of Oman. The sensor changed modes twice, and the spot blurred into the background. What created it is unknown.

records.title: DOW-UAP-PR121, Unresolved UAP Report, Gulf of Oman, 2021
records.summary_en: A video recorded from an aircraft’s screen shows moving blips disappearing at the edges and reappearing elsewhere. What produced them is unknown.

records.title: DOW-UAP-PR122, Unresolved UAP Report, Gulf of Oman, 2021
records.summary_en: A video recorded off an aircraft sensor display shows blips disappearing and returning from different directions. The report calls them “cold spheres,” but does not explain what they are.

records.title: DOW-UAP-PR123, Unresolved UAP Report, Pacific Ocean, 2019
records.summary_en: A bright spot fades into the background, then reappears in footage from a military sensor in the Pacific. The sensor moves closer, but the video does not reveal what the spot is.

records.title: DOW-UAP-PR124, Unresolved UAP Report, Pacific Ocean, 2019
records.summary_en: A 2019 video shows a prominent feature on a military sensor display. The sensor zooms in, and the feature becomes harder to make out. What the image shows is unknown.

records.title: DOW-UAP-PR125, Unresolved UAP Report, Pacific Ocean, 2019
records.summary_en: In a short military video from the Pacific, a mark nearly disappears into the background, then reappears. The sensor turns to track it, but what it is remains unknown.

records.title: DOW-UAP-PR126, Unresolved UAP Report, Pacific Ocean, 2019
records.summary_en: A U.S. service member filmed lights in the Pacific Ocean. The camera zoomed in on one, then pulled back, but the video was altered before it was submitted for review. The lights have not been identified.

records.title: DOW-UAP-PR127, Unresolved UAP Report, Pacific Ocean, 2019
records.summary_en: A U.S. service member filmed a light over the Pacific Ocean. The camera moves to follow it, and the image cuts out several times. The video was altered before it was submitted for review, but officials have not said what was changed.

records.title: DOW-UAP-PR134, Unresolved UAP Report, Middle East, 2025
records.summary_en: A military sensor tracked an area that appeared different from the background for about 90 seconds. The description details the sensor’s movements but does not identify what it captured.

records.title: DOW-UAP-PR136, Unresolved UAP Report, Middle East, 2023
records.summary_en: A military sensor tracked and zoomed in on a prominent feature in the image. A marker circled it briefly, then part of the aircraft blocked the view.

records.title: DOW-UAP-PR142, Unresolved UAP Report, Middle East, 2025
records.summary_en: A military video filmed in the Middle East shows a spot cross the frame and disappear. The report does not identify it.

records.title: DOW-UAP-PR149, Unresolved UAP Report, Middle East, 2023
records.summary_en: In military footage from the Middle East, a patch that looks different from the rest of the image crosses the screen. The sensor turns to follow it, but what the patch is remains unknown.

records.title: EOP-UAP-D001, NASC Inquiry into Bahia, Brazil Incident, November 13, 1963
records.summary_en: A radio station in Brazil reported a metal sphere with a human body inside. U.S. officials asked the embassy to check the story, and a telegram followed the next day.

records.title: FBI-UAP-D024, FD-302, “Airborne Lights and Triangle,” 2002, 2023-2024
records.summary_en: Two pilots watched a silent triangle pass over Bagram Air Base, blotting out the stars. Years later, the pilot searched for an explanation and found none.

records.title: FBI-UAP-D026, FD-302, “Dark Translucent Triangle,” 2023
records.summary_en: A couple in Colorado saw a nearly transparent triangle pass over their home. Just before it vanished, one side rose almost vertically without the object changing course.

records.title: FBI-UAP-D028, FD-302, “Dark Triangle with Lights,” 2011
records.summary_en: Two people described a black triangle flying low, making a pulsing hum, then vanishing before they could photograph it.

records.title: FBI-UAP-D030, FD-302, “Large Triangle with Red Lights,” 2023
records.summary_en: A man in Colorado Springs said he saw a black triangle with three red lights emerge from a gray cloud, accelerate, and disappear. When he looked back, the cloud was gone too.

records.title: FBI-UAP-D032, FD-302, “Slow-moving Objects,” 2026
records.summary_en: The FBI documented an interview about an incident in the western United States. A video filmed during the event was attached to the record, but the summary doesn’t say what happened or what the video shows.

records.title: FBI-UAP-D033, FD-302, “Thermally Elevated Aerial Object,” 2026
records.summary_en: A special agent described an incident in the western United States to the FBI, around 9 p.m. The summary says it may have been connected to something seen in the sky but never identified, but does not explain what happened.

records.title: FBI-UAP-D037, FD-302, “Multiple Red Lights,” 2026
records.summary_en: Two travelers saw red lights near the mountains. One watched a glow descend into a dry wash and move along it, then discovered his watch was 25 minutes fast.

records.title: FBI-UAP-D040, FD-302, “Multiple Red Lights,” 2026
records.summary_en: In the western United States, two travelers saw a red light moving over a ridge. About 15 minutes later, more lights appeared overhead. One dropped quickly and vanished, followed by the others.

records.title: FBI-UAP-PR007, “Slow-moving Objects,” 2026
records.summary_en: A U.S. agent recorded two dark areas moving slowly in a thermal image. The FBI summary does not identify them or explain what caused their movement.

records.title: DOW-UAP-D102, Project Blue Book File on Tremonton Film, Utah, 1952
records.summary_en: Delbert Newhouse filmed a group of lights near Tremonton, Utah. One object appeared to break away and vanish in the opposite direction. The Air Force later suggested they may have been seabirds reflecting sunlight.

records.title: DOW-UAP-D110, AAWSAP Statement of Objectives, July 2008
records.summary_en: A 2008 U.S. document called for research into future aviation technologies, including movement through space or time. It required the findings to be combined into an overall threat assessment, but does not say what researchers actually investigated.

records.title: DOW-UAP-D111, AAWSAP Solicitation and Original Order, September 2008
records.summary_en: In 2008, the U.S. government commissioned a study of potential hazards in aviation and aerospace. The contract covered 12 research areas, reports, and plans, but did not name the areas or describe the findings.

records.title: DOW-UAP-D117, AAWSAP DIRD, Metallic Glasses for Aerospace Applications, December 2009
records.summary_en: Metallic glass may be strong and easy to shape, but it is brittle. A 2009 document proposed combining it with a more flexible metal to improve its durability.

records.title: DOW-UAP-D129, AAWSAP DIRD, Metallic Spintronics, March 2010
records.summary_en: Researchers are investigating whether harnessing electrons’ magnetic properties could lead to faster, more energy-efficient components. Sensors based on the idea have already helped read data on hard drives, but more advanced applications still need development.

records.title: DOW-UAP-D154, Transcript of a Presentation by Captain Edward J. Ruppelt, 1952
records.summary_en: In 1952, Captain Edward Ruppelt presented a new review of about 800 reports. One in five remained unexplained, including reports from military personnel and pilots.

records.title: DOW-UAP-PR159, Historical Film of Reported UFOs, Utah, 1952
records.summary_en: Delbert Newhouse filmed lights in the sky near Tremonton, Utah. About 55 seconds in, the film cuts to sewing equipment. Why the two scenes appear on the same film remains unknown.

records.title: DOW-UAP-PR160, Presentation by Captain Edward J. Ruppelt, 1952
records.summary_en: The Air Force examined about 800 reports, and roughly one-fifth remained unexplained. In some cases, radar readings suggested extraordinary speeds, but the measurements were never confirmed.

records.title: LLE-UAP-PR001, Unresolved UAP Report, Colorado, 2023
records.summary_en: A Colorado officer filmed silent, colored lights and kept tracking them as he zoomed in and out. The video doesn’t reveal what produced the lights.

records.title: LLE-UAP-PR002, Unresolved UAP Report, Colorado, October 2023
records.summary_en: A Colorado officer filmed silent, flashing lights for 15 minutes. The camera tracked them, but their source remains unknown; the phone may have altered their appearance.

records.title: DOW-UAP-D103, Project Blue Book Photo File Relating to Tremonton Film, Utah, 1952
records.summary_en: Most reviewers thought the lights in the Utah footage were balloons. One representative thought they were too bright and moving too fast, and the Air Force later favored an explanation involving seabirds.

records.title: DOW-UAP-D104, Final Personnel Record for Newhouse, Delbert C., U.S. Navy, 1957
records.summary_en: Delbert Newhouse, an experienced Navy photographer, filmed near Tremonton, Utah. The Air Force examined the footage as part of a program investigating unidentified aerial phenomena.

records.title: DOW-UAP-D105, U.S. Air Force Flying Discs File, 1952
records.summary_en: A Navy pilot filmed objects near Tremonton, Utah, in July 1952. The Air Force assessed that they were probably seabirds, but the description does not say what appears in the footage.

records.title: DOW-UAP-D106, Mission Report, Iraq, 2022
records.summary_en: A military crew repeatedly spotted small objects during a mission over Iraq. It estimated their size and speed but could not determine their altitude or identify them.

records.title: DOW-UAP-D107, Mission Report, Middle East, 2025
records.summary_en: A U.S. military crew member in the Middle East reported seeing a white, round shape that he estimated was moving at up to about 800 kilometers per hour. The report was accompanied by heat-sensing footage, but doesn’t describe what appears in it.

records.title: DOW-UAP-D108, Mission Report, Middle East, 2025
records.summary_en: A U.S. military crew member reported seeing six small, round objects change direction quickly and simultaneously. The military report does not identify them.

records.title: DOW-UAP-D109, Mission Report, Middle East, 2022
records.summary_en: During a military mission in Iraq, an operator saw six round objects appear from time to time. When the operator returned the camera to previously scanned points, the objects appeared again, but their altitude and identity remained unknown.

records.title: DOW-UAP-D112, AAWSAP Contract Modification P00001, September 2009
records.summary_en: The research contract with Bigelow moved into another year, but payment depended on budget approval. The document does not identify the 12 research areas or report any findings.

records.title: DOW-UAP-D113, AAWSAP Contract Modification P00002, February 2010
records.summary_en: A 2010 document funded another year for a research program examining possible threats in aviation and space. It also said the lower-than-planned budget would affect reports and other work, without specifying how.

records.title: DOW-UAP-D114, AAWSAP Contract Modification P00003, May 2010
records.summary_en: A May 2010 contract amendment replaced the government representative overseeing a U.S. Department of Defense research program. The research itself did not change.

records.title: DOW-UAP-D115, AAWSAP Contract Modification P00004, May 2010
records.summary_en: A document from May 2010 recorded an update to the contract records of a U.S. research program focused on potential threats from space. It describes neither research nor a discovery, but an administrative change prompted by a change in the person responsible for the contract.

records.title: DOW-UAP-D116, AAWSAP Contract Modification P00005, September 2010
records.summary_en: A support contract for an aerospace research program was extended by three months, with no additional funding or change in scope.

records.title: DOW-UAP-D118, AAWSAP DIRD, Aerospace Applications of Programmable Matter, December 2009
records.summary_en: A 2009 document imagined spacecraft materials that could change how they function in response to software commands. Smart windows seemed more plausible than camouflage or invisibility.

records.title: DOW-UAP-D119, AAWSAP DIRD, Biomaterials, January 2010
records.summary_en: Medical materials must suit both the body and a device’s function. Rigorous safety testing slows progress, so many innovations rely on new uses for familiar materials.

records.title: DOW-UAP-D120, AAWSAP DIRD, Materials for Advanced Aerospace Platforms, January 2010
records.summary_en: A 2010 review concluded that no single material suits every aerospace vehicle. The choice depends on the design, operating conditions, and whether the material can be manufactured and tested.

records.title: DOW-UAP-D121, AAWSAP DIRD, Pulsed High-Power Microwave Source Technology, January 2010
records.summary_en: A military document reviewed a weapon that uses microwave pulses to disrupt computers. It cited a test in which navigation devices were reportedly disrupted, but offered no evidence that the weapon became a practical system.

records.title: DOW-UAP-D122, AAWSAP DIRD, Invisibility Cloaking Theory and Experiments, March 2010
records.summary_en: A 2010 review described experiments that partially concealed objects from microwaves, which are also used by radar. Perfect concealment is impractical under known physics, and there is still no practical way to hide an object from visible light.

records.title: DOW-UAP-D123, AAWSAP DIRD, Positron Aerospace Propulsion, March 2010
records.summary_en: A 2010 document examined positrons, particles of antimatter, as a way to propel aircraft and even carry a crew to Mars. Producing enough of them and storing them safely remain unsolved problems.

records.title: DOW-UAP-D124, AAWSAP DIRD, Space Access: Where We’ve Been and Where We Could Go, March 2010
records.summary_en: A 2010 report argued that reliance on single-use rockets made regular space travel difficult. It proposed a system for repeat trips, cargo transport, and in-orbit support.

records.title: DOW-UAP-D125, AAWSAP DIRD, Inertial Electrostatic Confinement Fusion, March 2010
records.summary_en: An electric method for fusing particles is nowhere near generating electricity, but it may provide particles for research.

records.title: DOW-UAP-D126, AAWSAP DIRD, Advanced Nuclear Propulsion for Manned Deep Space Missions, March 2010
records.summary_en: A 2010 document proposed propelling a spacecraft with tiny fusion explosions. A magnetic field would deflect the hot material, while a particle beam would trigger the blasts.

records.title: DOW-UAP-D127, AAWSAP DIRD, An Introduction to the Statistical Drake Equation, March 2010
records.summary_en: A document from a U.S. intelligence agency examined how to estimate how many civilizations could send and receive messages across the galaxy. Rather than offer a single number, it proposed calculating a range of possibilities.

records.title: DOW-UAP-D128, AAWSAP DIRD, Anomalous Acute and Subacute Field Effects on Human Biological Tissues, March 2010
records.summary_en: An intelligence document described three antenna engineers who fell ill within days of an unusual aerial incident. It proposed exposure to powerful fields as an explanation, but did not establish what happened or what caused their injuries.

records.title: DOW-UAP-D130, AAWSAP DIRD, Technological Approaches to Controlling External Devices, March 2010
records.summary_en: A 2010 report examined ways to control devices using signals from the brain and body. It estimated that, in the near term, the most practical methods would record signals from outside the body, including muscle signals. Faster, more precise control might require sensors implanted in the brain.

records.title: DOW-UAP-D131, AAWSAP DIRD, The Role of Superconductors in Gravity Research, March 2010
records.summary_en: A 2010 report surveyed studies investigating whether superconductors can affect gravity. It offered no proof, and the central claims have not been convincingly replicated.

records.title: DOW-UAP-D132, AAWSAP DIRD, Advanced Space Propulsion Based on Vacuum (Spacetime Metric) Engineering, March 2010
records.summary_en: A 2010 intelligence document explored whether changing space could help a spacecraft travel vast distances. It offered no way to do so, and the energy required far exceeds current capabilities.

records.title: DOW-UAP-D133, AAWSAP DIRD, The Space Communication Implications of Quantum Entanglement and Nonlocality, March 2010
records.summary_en: A document from the U.S. Department of Defense’s intelligence agency examined whether a connection between particles of light could let someone control a Mars rover without waiting for a signal. It proposed ways to test the idea but did not show that it works.

records.title: DOW-UAP-D134, AAWSAP DIRD, Maverick Inventor Versus Corporate Inventor: Where Will the Next Major Innovations Arise, March 2010
records.summary_en: A U.S. intelligence agency document asked who could deliver breakthroughs in energy and propulsion. It proposed researchers with technical training, equipment, and the freedom to change course.

records.title: DOW-UAP-D135, AAWSAP DIRD, Antigravity for Aerospace Applications, March 2010
records.summary_en: A 2010 intelligence report surveyed ideas for controlling gravity. One proposed a tiny, impossibly heavy sphere whose gravity would counteract Earth’s pull in the area beneath it. There is no practical way to create one today.

records.title: DOW-UAP-D136, AAWSAP DIRD, Biosensors and BioMEMS: A Survey of the Present Field, March 2010
records.summary_en: A 2010 document described a tiny device that sends an electrical signal to nerves and can pass through a syringe needle. The body can damage implanted devices, and sensors may become less accurate over time.

records.title: DOW-UAP-D137, AAWSAP DIRD, State of the Art and Evolution of High-Energy Lasers, March 2010
records.summary_en: A 2010 military report examined space-based laser weapons. The beam could travel without interference from air, but the spacecraft would need to supply power and carry equipment to manage the heat.

records.title: DOW-UAP-D138, AAWSAP DIRD, Warp Drive, Dark Energy, and the Manipulation of Extra Dimensions, April 2010
records.summary_en: A 2010 document proposed moving a spacecraft by changing the space around it. It linked dark energy to extra dimensions, but the idea rests on unproven assumptions.

records.title: DOW-UAP-D139, AAWSAP DIRD, Traversable Wormholes, Stargates, and Negative Energy, April 2010
records.summary_en: A U.S. intelligence agency document examined a theoretical tunnel spanning vast distances. A tiny effect observed in a laboratory is nowhere near enough to hold such a passage open.

records.title: DOW-UAP-D140, AAWSAP DIRD, High-Frequency Gravitational Wave Communications, April 2010
records.summary_en: A U.S. Department of Defense document examined whether high-frequency gravitational waves could carry messages without weakening like radio signals. The concept included secure communications and interplanetary navigation, but generating and detecting such waves have not been demonstrated.

records.title: DOW-UAP-D141, AAWSAP DIRD, Metamaterials for Aerospace Applications, April 2010
records.summary_en: A U.S. Department of Defense review examined artificial materials that might help lenses reveal tiny details and shrink components inside devices. The more advanced possibilities had yet to be convincingly demonstrated.

records.title: DOW-UAP-D142, AAWSAP DIRD, Concepts for Extracting Energy from the Quantum Vacuum, April 2010
records.summary_en: A 2010 intelligence report examined whether energy could be extracted from the vacuum, including to power or propel spacecraft. It described a force measured between metal plates but offered no practical way to generate useful energy from it.

records.title: DOW-UAP-D143, AAWSAP DIRD, Laser Lightcraft Nanosatellites, November 2010
records.summary_en: A 2010 document proposed using a remote laser to launch tiny satellites and give them a boost in orbit. Lightcraft vehicles were tested, but the material provided does not show that a satellite was launched into space this way.

records.title: DOW-UAP-D144, AAWSAP DIRD, Cockpits in the Era of Breakthrough Flight, November 2010
records.summary_en: A 2010 document imagined an aircraft that could move without banking. If people inside couldn’t feel it moving, the pilot would have to rely on screens.

records.title: DOW-UAP-D145, AAWSAP DIRD, Aneutronic Fusion Propulsion I, November 2010
records.summary_en: A U.S. document examined a space-engine concept based on the fusion of hydrogen and boron. The resulting particles could propel a spacecraft and generate electricity, but how to trigger the reaction under practical conditions remains unclear.

records.title: DOW-UAP-D146, AAWSAP DIRD, Aneutronic Fusion Propulsion II, November 2010
records.summary_en: A 2010 U.S. paper examined using fusion to propel spacecraft. The technology could be more powerful than conventional electric engines, but major challenges remain.

records.title: DOW-UAP-D147, AAWSAP DIRD, Ultracapacitors as Energy and Power Storage Devices, November 2010
records.summary_en: Ultracapacitors charge and discharge quickly, and can repeat the cycle hundreds of thousands of times. They store far less energy than batteries, so they’re best suited to brief bursts of extra power.

records.title: DOW-UAP-D148, AAWSAP DIRD, Detection and High-Resolution Tracking of Vehicles at Hypersonic Velocities, November 2010
records.summary_en: A 2010 U.S. document examined how to detect fast aircraft by the heat, shock waves, and turbulence they leave behind. It proposes combining several detection methods, since each picks up a different trace.

records.title: DOW-UAP-D149, AAWSAP DIRD, MHD Air Breathing Propulsion and Power for Aerospace Applications, November 2010
records.summary_en: A 2010 document concluded that the AJAX concept has little effect below Mach 12. Another idea aimed to create an air wall around an aircraft, but required a great deal of electricity.

records.title: DOW-UAP-D150, AAWSAP DIRD, Quantum Computing and Utilizing Organic Molecules in Automation Technology, December 2010
records.summary_en: A U.S. report proposed space computers made from DNA. Tiny machines might be able to repair damage, though it’s unclear how.

records.title: DOW-UAP-D151, AAWSAP DIRD, Cognitive Limits on Simultaneous Control of Multiple Unmanned Spacecraft, December 2010
records.summary_en: A 2010 document estimated how many spacecraft one person could manage: the more complex the missions, the fewer the number.

records.title: DOW-UAP-D152, AAWSAP DIRD, Negative Mass Propulsion, January 2011
records.summary_en: A U.S. intelligence agency document proposed digging a tunnel through the Moon to search for a theoretical material that might make spacecraft easier to propel.

records.title: DOW-UAP-D153, AAWSAP DIRD, Quantum Tomography of Negative Energy States in the Vacuum, January 2011
records.summary_en: A 2011 document proposed a way to measure and map tiny effects of negative energy in a laboratory. It linked them to warp drives but did not show that such drives could be built.

records.title: DOW-UAP-PR057b, "[Platform] Observes UAP in East China Sea 05 JAN 2023 INDOPACOM"
records.summary_en: Video from a military sensor over the Yellow Sea shows a feature blending into the background. The sensor zooms in, picks it up again, and tracks it, but what appears in the footage remains unknown.

records.title: DOW-UAP-PR130, Unresolved UAP Report, Iraq, 2022
records.summary_en: A military sensor image from Iraq shows an elongated shape with a trail. The mission report describes movement at varying speeds, but the trail may be an image-processing artifact.

records.title: DOW-UAP-PR131, Unresolved UAP Report, Iraq, 2022
records.summary_en: A military image from Iraq shows two spots, one with a streak. The mission report described movement at varying speeds, but the streak may be an artifact of image processing.

records.title: DOW-UAP-PR133, Unresolved UAP Report, Middle East, 2025
records.summary_en: A military camera tracked a bright dot for nearly five minutes as it slipped out of frame. The automatic tracking system couldn’t stay locked on, either.

records.title: DOW-UAP-PR135, Unresolved UAP Report, Middle East, 2025
records.summary_en: A military camera tracked moving areas in a video from the Middle East. A report described six spherical objects, but what they were is unknown.

records.title: DOW-UAP-PR140, Unresolved UAP Report, Middle East, 2022
records.summary_en: A military sensor tracked an area that looked different from its surroundings. When the camera switched imaging modes, the area left the frame—and the record does not identify it.

records.title: DOW-UAP-PR141, Unresolved UAP Report, Middle East, 2022
records.summary_en: A military camera tracked a spot that vanished from the screen and returned, while another appeared briefly. The footage doesn’t reveal what caused them.

records.title: DOW-UAP-PR143, Unresolved UAP Report, Yellow Sea, 2023
records.summary_en: An infrared sensor aboard a U.S. military platform tracked an area that looked different from its surroundings for 19 seconds. The record does not identify what was there.

records.title: DOW-UAP-PR144, Unresolved UAP Report, Yellow Sea, 2023
records.summary_en: A military sensor tracked a spot over the Yellow Sea, but the footage doesn’t identify what caused it.

records.title: DOW-UAP-PR148, Unresolved UAP Report, East China Sea, 2023
records.summary_en: A military sensor tracked a patch of the image that looked different from its surroundings, zoomed in, and kept tracking it. The description does not say what was there.

records.title: DOW-UAP-PR150, Unresolved UAP Report, Yellow Sea, 2023
records.summary_en: A military sensor over the Yellow Sea tracked a spot that looked different from its surroundings. Near the end of the video, the platform carrying the sensor blocked the right side of the frame.

records.title: DOW-UAP-PR151, Unresolved UAP Report, Yellow Sea, 2023
records.summary_en: A military sensor over the Yellow Sea tracked an area that looked different from its surroundings, zoomed in on it for a few seconds, and continued tracking it. The report does not identify what appeared there.

records.title: DOW-UAP-PR152, Unresolved UAP Report, Yellow Sea, 2023
records.summary_en: In 2023, an infrared sensor recorded an area in the Yellow Sea that looked different from its surroundings and tracked it for 1 minute and 38 seconds. The record describes the tracking but doesn’t identify what was in the area.

records.title: LLE-UAP-D001, Transcript of an Unresolved UAP Report, Colorado, October 2023
records.summary_en: A Colorado police officer recorded a video, but the released record contains only a partial transcript. The audio and redacted passages were withheld to protect privacy and sensitive information.

records.title: LLE-UAP-D002, Transcript of an Unresolved UAP Report, Colorado, October 2023
records.summary_en: A Colorado police officer filmed a light that appeared to rise above a power line and approach him. He said a similar light shone red and blue into his patrol car the night before.

records.title: LLE-UAP-D003, Transcript of an Unresolved UAP Report, Colorado, October 2023
records.summary_en: A Colorado officer recorded a video, but the transcript doesn’t describe what appears in it. The audio was removed, and the transcript notes only indistinct background noise.

records.title: LLE-UAP-D004, Transcript of an Unresolved UAP Report, Colorado, January 2024
records.summary_en: A Colorado officer reported that a ball of light hung in the sky for about 15 minutes. He later said it was moving toward him, but the transcript doesn’t say what happened next.

records.title: LLE-UAP-PR003, Unresolved UAP Report, Colorado, October 2023
records.summary_en: A Colorado police officer reported a silent light flashing red, blue, and green. The phone zoomed in, but the source of the light remains unidentified.

records.title: LLE-UAP-PR004, Unresolved UAP Report, Colorado, January 2024
records.summary_en: A Colorado officer filmed red, blue, and green lights he described as silent. Cars approached; the phone adjusted its focus, but the camera stayed trained on the lights.

records.title: DOW-UAP-D176, Triangular UAP AARO Memorandum for Record, 2026
records.summary_en: Two agents described a triangular object that ascended, halted, and descended into a canyon. A search of the accessible area found no debris or impact marks.

records.title: FBI-UAP-D043, FD-302, Unidentified Aerial Object Observation Report, 2026
records.summary_en: The FBI documented an interview with two agents regarding an incident reported at a security site in the Western United States. The document does not describe what was seen or what occurred at the location.

records.title: DOW-UAP-D174, Utah Ranch Investigation Report, April 2010
records.summary_en: Researchers in Utah heard reports of creatures and lights, and sought to collect photos, recordings, and samples. They planned to attempt contact with what they believed was behind the reports, but it's unknown if they ever did.

records.title: DOW-UAP-D155, Air Intelligence Information Report, Saudi Arabia, 1957
records.summary_en: A B-52 crew identified a blip on their targeting screen over Saudi Arabia for approximately five to seven minutes. The blip was smaller than a signal received from another aircraft in the area, but the report doesn't explain its origin.

records.title: DOW-UAP-D177, Unresolved UAP Report, Catalina Island, 1955
records.summary_en: Paul J. Carr of Avalon reported seeing a bright orange object in the Catalina sky one evening, the size of a coin at arm's length. The assessment suggested it might have been a natural celestial object, but no further investigation was conducted.

records.title: DOW-UAP-D178, Unresolved UAP Report, Catalina Island, 1953
records.summary_en: A round, purple-white object was seen over Catalina Island, remained stationary, then moved toward Los Angeles. Astronomers suggested it might have been Jupiter, but the report didn't explain the movement.

records.title: DOW-UAP-D179, Air Intelligence Information Report, Catalina Island, 1952
records.summary_en: Three Boy Scout campers at a summer camp on Catalina Island reported seeing silver discs. One of the objects climbed rapidly and appeared to break apart, but the officer who recorded the report did not verify the story's credibility.

records.title: DOW-UAP-D181, Unresolved UAP Report, Catalina Island, 1949
records.summary_en: On April 28, 1949, Percy Waki's wife and another individual reported seeing six objects over Catalina Island. The US Air Force determined there wasn't enough information to assess the incident.

records.title: DOW-UAP-D042, Range Fouler Debrief, Arabian Gulf, 2023
records.summary_en: A US military operator in the Arabian Gulf reported three objects circling each other. One passed through a screen, and another bypassed it at a higher speed.

records.title: DOW-UAP-D156, Air Intelligence Information Report, Guam, 1956
records.summary_en: A pilot near Guam reported a flashing light. An Air Force report suggested it might have been related to a weather balloon, if the balloon malfunctioned and stayed low.

records.title: DOW-UAP-D157, Air Intelligence Information Report, Italy, 1952
records.summary_en: A professor near Sassari described a blue-green sphere that rapidly crossed the sky, vanished, and then reappeared. The US Air Force documented the report but offered no explanation for the sphere.

records.title: DOW-UAP-D158, Flying Object Report, Canada, 1953
records.summary_en: Three US Air Force personnel in British Columbia reported a blinking light that descended, stopped, ascended again, and then moved westward.

records.title: DOW-UAP-D159, Air Intelligence Information Report, Germany, 1953
records.summary_en: A British pilot reported red rockets in front of his plane en route to Berlin. Later, a steady red light was reported in the area, but another pilot did not see it.

records.title: DOW-UAP-D160, Air Intelligence Information Report, Morocco, 1953
records.summary_en: A radar crew in Morocco observed a signature that changed shape from V to W to M, then faded. Air Force personnel offered several explanations but did not determine its origin.

records.title: DOW-UAP-D161, Air Intelligence Information Report, Alaska, 1953
records.summary_en: An Alaskan island resident saw a small light on the edge of what was then a Soviet island. It lasted a few seconds, and the report doesn't explain its origin.

records.title: DOW-UAP-D162, Air Intelligence Information Report, Alaska, 1953
records.summary_en: An Alaskan sergeant with the local military force saw a steady light on the horizon near Gambell. It disappeared as if extinguished; the report suggested a ship might have created it, but its source was not determined.

records.title: DOW-UAP-D163, Air Intelligence Information Report, Sweden, 1953
records.summary_en: Two crew members on a passenger plane in Sweden reported a metallic object that rapidly approached them and vanished within seconds. The Air Force identified no Swedish aircraft in the area, and the radar check results are not included in the report.

records.title: DOW-UAP-D164, Flying Object Report, Indiana, 1953
records.summary_en: Two reporters traveling near Seymour, Indiana, reported white, cloud-like objects with points of light inside them and a blue-white trail behind them. They described the objects approaching, stopping in place, and then sharply moving away upwards.

records.title: DOW-UAP-D166, MUFON Reports Prepared for BAASS, November 2008
records.summary_en: MUFON prepared papers on future aviation for a research firm. The collection presented unidentified object reports as a source of information for examining aviation capabilities.

records.title: DOW-UAP-D167, Project Capella, December 2008
records.summary_en: A 2008 report proposed compiling and organizing reports of anomalous aerial phenomena for research. It is unknown if the database was ever built.

records.title: DOW-UAP-D168, BAASS Project Management Plan, December 2008
records.summary_en: BAASS proposed focusing government research on several aircraft and events it deemed anomalous. The document outlines the proposal but doesn't detail what was investigated or found.

records.title: DOW-UAP-D169, BAASS Monthly Report, March 2009
records.summary_en: A 2009 report describes a company that developed a system to centralize reports of unidentified aerial observations. It sought to become the official reporting channel for the US Aviation Authority.

records.title: DOW-UAP-D170, BAASS Monthly Report, April 2009
records.summary_en: BAASS acquired data on MUFON reports and prepared a small team for field investigations, alongside arrangements for material analysis.

records.title: DOW-UAP-D171, BAASS Monthly Report, June 2009
records.summary_en: BAASS expanded its team and offices, investigated reports received via MUFON, and sent a team to Brazil. Concurrently, it proposed reducing the monthly payment to the organization, subject to further review.

records.title: DOW-UAP-D173, BAASS Monthly Report, November 2009
records.summary_en: A report by Bigelow Aerospace documented investigations at a Utah ranch, a separate database for incidents in the area, and an initial report of a blue orb.

records.title: DOW-UAP-D175, BAASS Self-Assessment of UAP Analysis Capabilities, November 2010
records.summary_en: In 2010, BAASS presented case studies and computer simulations to demonstrate its methods for analyzing unidentified phenomena. The company asserted that this analysis could aid in developing aviation and defense technologies, thereby strengthening its argument for continued involvement in a government program.

records.title: DOW-UAP-D180, Final Personnel Record for McCoy, Howard M., U.S. Air Force, 1954
records.summary_en: Colonel Howard McCoy was involved in the planning and operation of two Air Force programs investigating unidentified phenomena. His service record does not detail what they examined or discovered.

records.title: EOP-UAP-D002, Memorandum on Interagency Coordination for the Recovery of Foreign Materiel, May 1963
records.summary_en: In 1963, US officials proposed NASA assist in the covert collection of sensitive space equipment in foreign countries. A senior NASA official opposed the proposal, but it's unknown if it was carried out.

records.title: USG-UAP-D002, Interagency Correspondence Concerning Space Fragments, 1962-1964
records.summary_en: For nearly two years, U.S. officials discussed how to handle materials related to space activity. They planned to tell the public NASA would store them, but private communications also discussed their analysis.
